title: Experts disagree on deferCompletionForBackgroundStage
context:
Chief architect: Ruled by the chief, settled by the run evidence: one predicate answers "is a stage of this change still running" for the verify backstop, receipt, cost seal and HUD verdict, and that predicate must say yes on EITHER signal: the turn-end payload lists a paqad stage agent of the open change, OR the stage ledger has an open stage_start with a dispatched stage agent and no stage_end and no agent stop. The verdict landed 27 s before the first payload naming the planning agent, so the payload alone is not enough. Only stage helpers count; a non-stage background helper does not hold the verdict back. Deferral ends when the agent stops, and the next turn end judges as before.

Target: deferCompletionForBackgroundStage
- solution-architect: Reuse this one predicate as the single answer to 'is a stage of this change still running' for every turn-end path (the verify backstop, receipt sealing, cost window sealing and the HUD verdict) instead of adding a second check; today the Stop hooks return early when the payload's background_tasks is empty, so a stage that the stage ledger shows started and not ended with a dispatched stage agent is still judged.
- solution-architect: The running-stage decision must also hold from the stage ledger alone (an open stage_start with no stage_end and no SubagentStop for its stage agent), not only from the Stop payload, because the run shows the verdict landing 27 s before the first payload that named the background planning agent.
